summary: This Dockerfile builds an Ubuntu container with SSH client tools and a custom interactive SSH launcher. It installs necessary packages (fzf for fuzzy finding, perl for parsing), sets up SSH configuration files organized in a modular way, and adds a sophisticated bash function that lets you search and connect to SSH hosts with colored documentation displayed as you type.

explanations.3: This tells Ubuntu's package installer to run in non-interactive mode so it won't prompt for user input during installation.
explanations.7: Ubuntu's default package sources only include 'main' and 'restricted' repositories, but fzf is in 'universe', so this command adds those additional repositories before installing packages.
explanations.10: The --no-install-recommends flag skips optional packages that normally come with these tools, keeping the image smaller.
explanations.14: After installing packages, this deletes the package cache files that are no longer needed, reducing the final image size.
explanations.17: This creates the directory structure for modular SSH config files and sets restrictive permissions (700 means only root can read/write/execute) for security.
explanations.52: The > redirects all those printf lines into a single file; this creates an SSH config file with two host definitions.
explanations.66: chmod 600 sets read/write permissions only for the owner; SSH requires strict permissions on config files for security.
explanations.103: The perl -ne reads the SSH config files line-by-line and processes them with the script inside the quoted block.
explanations.111: $buf accumulates comment lines, separated by ;;; when a Host line is found, the comments are attached to that host.
explanations.134: The 150-space padding creates invisible space in the output so that when fzf displays results, the description (shown in the preview) doesn't run into the visible columns.
explanations.136: The backslash continues the command on the next line; the closing quote ends the Perl script so fzf can process its output.
explanations.137: fzf's --query flag pre-filters results based on the first argument passed to sshf() function.
explanations.139: The --delimiter tells fzf to split each line at ##### so it treats the alias/hostname as searchable columns and the description as preview-only.
explanations.146: The --preview command runs when you hover over an entry; it extracts column 2 (the description with formatting tags) and converts the tags to ANSI color codes.
explanations.160: ssh -G shows the computed SSH configuration for an alias, resolving any defaults or config file settings so we can display exactly what will be used.
explanations.176: This adds a custom command prompt that displays a whale emoji and shows the current user and directory, making it visually clear you're in a container.
explanations.178: CMD specifies what runs when the container starts; -i flag makes bash interactive so you get a shell prompt.
